summary:
Roughly $750 billion. That’s how much Meta Platforms Inc., Amazon.com Inc., Microsoft Corp. and Google owner Alphabet Inc. are expected to devote to capital expenditures this year alone.

That’s more than the entire gross domestic product of Ireland or Belgium. More than half of what all of the companies in the S&P 500 Index spent in total last year. title: Wald: Middle East Risks Keep Oil’s Risk Premium in Place
title_cn: Wald: Middle East Risks Keep Oil’s Risk Premium in Place
summary: Ellen Wald, president of Transversal Consulting and nonresident senior fellow at the Atlantic Council Global Energy Center, says she sees no recent move by the president that could materially bring down oil prices. She says short-lived dips driven by statements or social media have not lasted, and the market has largely shed expectations that the conflict will soon end. Wald says oil-market buffers built up over the prior six months are nearly exhausted, while reported oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz—including ship-to-ship transfers—may not be sustainable. She speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Miller Warns US-Saudi Strikes May Not Stop Houthis

He notes that US forces previously conducted more than a thousand strikes on Houthi facilities, but argues airstrikes are unlikely to change the group’s political calculations. Miller says Saudi infrastructure is especially vulnerable because the Houthis have demonstrated the ability to strike airports and oil facilities. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
